title: Google Service Account
description: A Google Cloud service-account key, used to call Google APIs as a machine identity. Paste the JSON file downloaded from Google Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Keys → Add key, verbatim, under serviceAccountJSON. Creating the key is only half of access: for Google Analytics the service account's client_email must ALSO be added as a property user in Google Analytics → Admin → Property Access Management, which is a separate product and a separate step.

serviceAccountJSON.title: Service Account Key JSON
serviceAccountJSON.description: The downloaded key file, verbatim. Must contain client_email and private_key. The private_key is a multi-line PEM block; if your paste turned its newlines into literal \n escapes, that is tolerated and converted.

type.title: Type
type.description: Always 'service_account' for a key of this kind.

project_id.title: Project ID
project_id.description: The Google Cloud project that owns the service account. Informational — the API being called is authorized by the key, not by this field.

client_email.title: Client Email
client_email.description: The service account's identity, e.g. mj-analytics@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com. This is the address to grant access to on the target Google Analytics property.

private_key_id.title: Private Key ID
private_key_id.description: Identifier of this specific key. Useful when rotating: it names which key a Cloud Console entry corresponds to.

private_key.title: Private Key
private_key.description: The PEM-encoded RSA private key, beginning '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----'. Secret.
